sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Amoghasiddhi** ​(*amoghasiddhi*) — ‌Infallible ‌Success, North ​· ​'Unfailing Accomplishment' ​— ​the fifth ​Dhyānibuddha, lord ‌of ​the karma ​family ‌— belongs ​to ‌the Buddhist ​tradition, ‌where it ​is ​catalogued under ​the ​domain "Infallible ​Success, ‌North". The ​name means ‌"'Unfailing ​Accomplishment' — ‌the ​fifth Dhyānibuddha, ‌lord ​of the ‌karma ​family".

**Amoghasiddhi** ​is ‌infallible success, ‌north. ‌The name ​means ​"'Unfailing Accomplishment' ‌— the ​fifth ​Dhyānibuddha, lord ‌of ​the karma ​family" ‌and belongs ​to ‌the buddhist ​tradition.

​PuniCodex restores ​the ​name as ‌**Amoghasiddhi** and ‌serves ​its temple ‌at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/amoghasiddhi/). ​The ‌restoration needs ‌no ‌distinctive letters ‌or ​diacritics its ‌ASCII ​form would ​lose, ​which places ‌the name ​in ​Tier 2. ​The ‌plain ASCII ​form ​*amoghasiddhi* survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ‌imposed by ​the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ‌not the ​fallback, ​is the ​form ​the project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Devanagari as ​**अमोघसिद्धि**. Etymologically ​it ​means "'Unfailing ​Accomplishment' — ​the fifth ‌Dhyānibuddha, lord ​of the ​karma ‌family".

The ​ASCII form ‌*amoghasiddhi* survives ​only because ‌the ​early domain-name ​system could ​not carry ​diacritics; it ​is a ‌technological ​compromise, not ‌an ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode restoration ​**Amoghasiddhi** ‌recovers the ​full diacritic ‌detail of ​the scholarly ​transliteration directly ‌in ‌the address ‌bar. The ​restoration needs ​no distinctive ‌letters ​or diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form would ​lose, which ​places the ‌name ​in Tier ‌2.

The ​letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

- ​**a** ​→ **A** ‌— Same, ‌capitalized
- ​**m** → ‌**m** — ​Same
​- **o** ‌→ **o** ‌— Same
‌- **g** ‌→ ​**g** — ‌Same
- ​**h** → ​**h** — ​Same
- ‌**a** ​→ **a** ​— Same
​- **s** ‌→ **s** ​— ​Same
- ​**i** → ‌**i** — ​Same
- ‌**d** → ​**d** ‌— Same
​- **d** ‌→ **d** ‌— Same
​- ​**h** → ​**h** — ​Same
- ‌**i** → ‌**i** — ​Same

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/amoghasiddhi/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**amoghasiddhi** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Amoghasiddhi.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"amoghasiddhi" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Amoghasiddhi".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"amoghasiddhi" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Amoghasiddhi" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Amoghasiddhi was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Amoghasiddhi ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Amoghasiddhi ‌place infallible ​success, ​north at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### Origins ‌(Myth)

​Amoghasiddhi appears ‌in ​buddhist tradition ‌as ​infallible success, ​north. ​The name's ​meaning, ​"'Unfailing Accomplishment' ‌— ​the ‌fifth Dhyānibuddha, ​lord ‌of the ​karma ‌family", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ​this figure.

‌### ‌Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ​and ‌later tradition-keepers ​preserved ​Amoghasiddhi in ‌ritual, ​text, and ​iconography, ‌ensuring the ​name ‌survived into ​the ​modern scholarly ​record.

​The myths ‌of ‌Amoghasiddhi survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ​and ​later retellings. ‌Each ‌version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ​its ‌tellers — ​poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ‌scholars. ​The PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ‌privilege ​a single ​version; ​it gathers ‌the ​attestations so ‌that ​readers can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Amoghasiddhi gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Amoghasiddhi ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming अमोघसिद्धि, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to infallible ​success ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate Amoghasiddhi ‌is ‌to ​hold the ​idea ​of infallible ​Success, ​North in ‌the ​mind ​and to ‌ask ​what of ‌it ​endures. The ‌name ​means ​"'Unfailing Accomplishment' ​— ​the fifth ​Dhyānibuddha, ‌lord ​of the ‌karma ​family" — ‌and ​a name ‌that ​carries ‌its meaning ​so ​openly invites ‌meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ​recollection. ​The tradition ‌remembers ​the name ​as ‌infallible ​Success, North ​· ‌'Unfailing Accomplishment' ​— ‌the fifth ​Dhyānibuddha, ​lord ​of the ​karma ‌family.

Sit ‌with ​the ‌restored form ​— ​Amoghasiddhi — ‌and ‌the diacritics ‌themselves ‌become ​the practice: ‌each ​mark is ​a ​small act ‌of ​attention, ​a refusal ​to ‌let the ​plain ​ASCII ​form *amoghasiddhi* ‌stand ​in for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved in ‌this ​name, the ​restoration ​asks the ​reader ‌to ‌preserve in ​turn.
